memory_lessons.applicability: Scalar table-loop unrolling on this workload; compare against the measured baseline before assuming reduced loop control helps.
memory_lessons.claim: The prior two-group candidate passed the recorded correctness cases but averaged 82.32 µs, slower than the baseline’s 55.00 µs. Greater unrolling is a distinct test, not evidence of improvement; compiler/code-size effects remain unknown.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this four-group schedule under the same native protocol and retain it only if correctness and repeated timings justify it.

proposal.hypothesis: The only measured unroll candidate so far—two 8-character groups—was correct but slower than baseline (82.32 µs versus 55.00 µs mean). This contrasting four-group schedule computes each group’s table lookups before validating the group, then validates all four before writing output. It may expose more independent lookup work and amortize loop control, but code size and register pressure may make it slower still. No speedup is assumed.

retained: Added a scalar helper that performs all eight table lookups for one 8-character block before validating the lookup values.
Unrolled the decode loop to load and decode four independent blocks per iteration, followed by one combined validity decision and ordered output stores.
Set the bulk guard to 37 remaining characters so the loop reads only 32 input characters while preserving the original five-character tail margin.
Retained the original bytewise decoder for invalid input, padding, and remaining tails; added no explicit SIMD or parallel execution.
